rows.narrative:
Chester County Schools will utilize Title I funds from the 1% required family engagement set-aside to finance stipends for Family Engagement Coordinators at each Title I school building.

These individuals will support the district's family engagement initiatives by coordinating activities, communicating with families, and promoting stronger home-school connections.

The total amount allocated for Family Engagement stipends is $7034. 

Required employer-paid benefits associated with these stipends are budgeted separately and reflected
in budget codes 201, 204, and 212.

All of these funds are accounted for on the District Set-Aside page.

Chester County Schools will utilize Title I funds to cover the employer's required Social Security contributions for professional employees who earn stipends as school-level Family Engagement Coordinators or for preparing and leading parent involvement sessions.

A total of $398.99 will be funded from the additional family engagement set-aside. These funds cover the employer's share of Social Security expenses associated with family engagement stipends and ensure full compliance with federal employment obligations.

All of these funds are reflected on the District Set-Aside page.

This investment supports the district's goal of strengthening family-school partnerships to promote student academic achievement and aligns with the Title I purpose of increasing meaningful parental involvement.

Funds allocated for instructional supplies and materials will be used to support high-quality, standards-aligned instruction across New Heights School programs. These resources will directly enhance classroom teaching and learning by providing educators and students with the tools necessary to engage in rigorous academic work aligned to Tennessee State Standards.

Instructional supplies may include, but are not limited to, consumable classroom materials, supplemental curriculum resources, intervention materials, and instructional manipulatives in core content areas such as English language arts and mathematics. Materials will be selected based on identified student needs, local assessment data, and alignment to district and school improvement goals.

These resources will support differentiated instruction within Tier I classrooms, as well as targeted interventions for students who require additional academic support. By equipping teachers with appropriate materials, the district ensures that all students have access to meaningful learning experiences that promote academic growth and achievement.

All purchases will be reasonable, necessary, and aligned to federal guidelines, ensuring that funds are used to supplement, not supplant, existing resources. The district will monitor the use of instructional supplies to ensure effectiveness and alignment with intended outcomes.
